faq.q: Why does the Moon change shape?
faq.a: The Moon does not really change. The Sun always lights half of it, and as the Moon orbits the Earth we see different amounts of that lit half, so it looks like it changes shape.
asks: What are the phases of the Moon?

faq.a: Waxing means growing. A waxing Moon shows a bigger lit part each night, from new moon to full moon.
Waning means shrinking. A waning Moon shows a smaller lit part each night, from full moon back to new moon.

faq.q: How long is the Moon's cycle?
faq.a: From one new moon to the next takes about 29 and a half days, roughly one month.
asks: How often is there a full moon?

faq.q: Why can we not see the new moon?
faq.a: At new moon, the Moon is between the Earth and the Sun, so its sunny side faces away from us and the side facing us is dark.

facts: The cycle of lunar phases (synodic month) lasts about 29.5 days.
The Islamic, Hindu and Chinese calendars use the Moon's phases to set festivals such as Eid, Diwali and Chinese New Year.

quiz.say: The lit part of the Moon gets bigger each night. What is it doing?
quiz.show: When the lit part grows, the Moon is…
quiz.why: Waxing means the lit part is growing towards full moon.

wrong.2: Its spin does not change; we just see more of its sunny side.

quiz.say: About how long does the Moon take to go through all its phases?
quiz.show: One full cycle of phases takes about…
quiz.why: From new moon to new moon takes about 29 and a half days.

wrong.0: In one day the Moon's shape hardly changes.
wrong.2: In one year there are about twelve full cycles.
